page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by a 3.0 GHz Ampere Altra processor utilizing the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading performance degradation. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the t2a-standard-2 sits primarily in the lower tiers of compute and memory throughput. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the average range. However, multi-core and memory-intensive operations show limitations, with Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU scores falling into the poor category. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, peaking at 139.93 GB/sec for cached small blocks and dropping to 26.99 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides a resource-dense, low-overhead hardware profile suitable for budget-conscious deployments. Due to its modest multi-threaded performance and lack of local storage, this instance is best suited for lightweight workloads. Recommended use cases include static web serving, basic text processing, software compilation testing, and small-scale database or caching operations like Redis.
